purpose: Econazole nitrate is a cream applied to the skin to treat fungal infections like athlete's foot, jock itch, ringworm, and yeast infections of the skin. It helps clear up the rash, itching, and irritation caused by these infections. Your doctor may also prescribe it for a skin condition called tinea versicolor, which causes patchy skin discoloration.
how_it_works: This medication works by attacking the outer layer of the fungus, called the cell membrane. It blocks the fungus from making a substance it needs to survive, causing it to break down and die. Over time, this stops the infection from spreading and allows your skin to heal.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this cream well. Some people may notice mild burning, stinging, itching, or redness right where they apply it. These reactions are usually minor and go away on their own as your skin adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not use this cream in or near your eyes, mouth, or vagina unless your doctor specifically tells you to. If you develop severe skin irritation, a rash, or signs of an allergic reaction like swelling or difficulty breathing, stop using it and contact your doctor right away. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before using this medication.
typical_dosing: For most skin infections, apply a thin layer of the cream to the affected area once or twice daily, as directed by your doctor. Keep using it for the full prescribed time, even if your skin starts to look better early, to make sure the infection is completely gone. Treatment usually lasts 2 to 4 weeks depending on the type of infection.
